posts.html:
Set the title, audience, and identity for your new publication.

Choose a publication name

Use the name readers will recognize on the site and in their inbox. Add a one-sentence description that says what you publish and who it is for.

Check your address

Open the public URL in a private window. Use that address wherever you link to the publication.

Create your first draft

Outline one useful idea. Give it a descriptive title, add a short introduction, and split the body into sections a reader can scan.

  • Use a title you can say aloud.
  • Describe what readers will learn.
  • Open your publication on a small screen.

Review and publish

Read the draft aloud, check its links, and preview it at the width your readers are likely to use.

Send the public link to one trusted reader and ask them to follow the guide from start to finish.

posts.html:
Structure instructions around the task a reader wants to complete.

State what readers need

List any access, materials, or earlier steps a reader needs before starting.

Write one action per step

Start with a verb, name the control or location, and describe the result when it helps readers verify their progress.

Describe the result

End by showing what success looks like and where the reader can go next.

posts.html:
Decide which topics appear and set their reading order.

Choose a primary tag

Make each guide’s main topic its primary public tag. Add a short tag description for the section card.

Set the section sequence

Enter the tag slugs in the Sections setting, separated by commas. List the first section you want readers to see first.

Check the section cards

Open the homepage and confirm each card points to the expected section and starter guides.

posts.html:
Refer to guides with the same addresses readers see in the contents tree.

Read an article number

An address such as 2.3 means the third guide in the second section.

Pair numbers with titles

Use the article title or link alongside its number so readers can find it quickly.

Check after reordering

Section and article numbers follow the current reading order. Update references in any material that quotes the old numbers.

Summarize the problem

Name the page or task and describe the result you expected.

Copy the article or heading link so the person responding can find the same instructions.

posts.html:
Give readers a destination when a guide does not answer their question.

Choose a contact destination

Use a contact page that explains how to get help or an email address your team checks.

Set the Support URL

Add the destination in the theme settings. Handbook uses it in the header, on the homepage, and after a negative feedback answer.

Test the destination

Open the support link as a reader and confirm it reaches the intended page or email address.

Check publication status, tags, and the theme’s section list.

Confirm the guide is public

Open its public address in a private browser window and confirm it is available to the intended audience.

Check the primary tag

Make sure the first tag is the public section you want the guide to appear under.

Review the Sections setting

If the list is configured, confirm it includes the exact slug of the guide’s primary tag.
